questions.question:
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
You might think "Hey, these are exceptional people." However, we are all born with the potential for resilience. Just like these people, we all can develop the strength to quickly recover from a crisis that could otherwise cause lasting damage to our mental health. The good news is that resilience is like a muscle. You can build it up through practice, by developing thoughts, behaviors, and habits that allow you to recover from painful or stressful events. Here are three basic strategies to build up this "resilience muscle." First, accept and respect adversity as a natural part of life. This doesn't mean being passive, but understanding that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress. Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, "Why me?", you can face whatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can't. Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process. Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity!
choices: ① How long does it usually take to build up the "resilience muscle"?
② What is resilience compared to in the passage?
③ What does accepting adversity not mean?
④ What should we focus on instead of asking "Why me?"
⑤ How can embracing challenges help us?
questions.why: 글에는 회복력이 근육과 같아서 '연습으로(through practice)' 키울 수 있다는 말만 있고, 얼마나 걸리는지는 나오지 않는다. quickly recover는 위기에서 '빨리 회복한다'는 뜻이지 근육을 키우는 기간이 아니다.
questions.wrong: ② like a muscle, ③ This doesn't mean being passive, ④ focus on what you can change, ⑤ confront them as a learning process에서 각각 답을 찾을 수 있다.

questions.question:
현미경에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
For a microscope to function properly, it must meet certain minimum requirements. These include an eyepiece, a tube through which the viewer looks, and a lens for magnification. The microscope must also have a component that can hold a specimen and move from side to side to explore different areas of the specimen. Furthermore, a mechanism to bring the specimen into focus, usually accomplished by moving it closer to or farther from the lens, is necessary. Finally, a light source is required to illuminate the specimen. An ideal microscope would be made with the best performing materials and mechanisms for each component. However, such a microscope would likely be enormously expensive. On the other hand, a cheap microscope may not be able to deliver high performance. Prakash and Cybulski experimented with various designs and materials in order to find a suitable compromise. While many manufacturers might have settled for a middle ground between these two extremes, Prakash and Cybulski were determined to create a microscope that was both inexpensive and high-performing, while remaining accessible to all.
choices: ① 현미경에는 시료를 고정하고 좌우로 움직이는 부품이 있어야 한다.
② 초점은 보통 시료를 렌즈에 가깝게 하거나 멀게 하여 맞춘다.
③ 시료를 비추는 광원이 필요하다.
④ Prakash와 Cybulski는 다른 제조업체들처럼 가격과 성능의 중간 수준에 만족하기로 했다.
⑤ 최고의 재료로 만든 이상적인 현미경은 매우 비쌀 것이다.
questions.why: 마지막 문장에서 많은 제조업체는 중간 지점(middle ground)에 만족했겠지만, 두 사람은 '싸면서도 성능이 좋은' 현미경을 만들기로 결심했다(were determined). 중간 수준에 만족한 것이 아니다.
questions.wrong: ① hold a specimen and move from side to side, ② moving it closer to or farther from the lens, ③ a light source, ⑤ enormously expensive와 일치한다. 앞 문장의 compromise만 보고 ④를 고르지 않도록 주의.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 표현의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
I am not saying that these strategies are easy or remove all stress and suffering. Still, I urge you to practice them whenever you can, particularly when you are ①<u>under stress</u>. Remember that there is ②<u>no better time</u> to build your "resilience muscle" than the moment when you are in the middle of adversity and uncertainty. Practicing resilience during tough times helps you ③<u>stay in your comfort zone</u> and grow stronger. However, you can also apply these strategies to everyday small stresses or minor challenges. Then you will gradually become ④<u>more able to deal with</u> big ones. Resilient people tend to be happier and more fulfilled because they are ⑤<u>less afraid of</u> failing or challenges. So, building resilience is the key not only to overcoming adversity but also to living a happy life.
questions.why: 힘든 시기에 회복력을 연습하면 '견디고(endure)' 더 강해진다는 흐름이다. stay in your comfort zone(안전지대에 머물다)은 도전을 피한다는 뜻이라 grow stronger와 맞지 않는다.
questions.wrong: ① 스트레스를 받을 때, ② 역경 한가운데가 '가장 좋은' 때, ④ 큰 스트레스에도 더 잘 대처, ⑤ 실패를 덜 두려워함 — 모두 흐름에 맞다. comfort zone은 같은 과 Further Reading에서 고정 마인드셋을 설명할 때 나온 표현이다.

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] Such a low price is possible because the whole device is folded from a single flat sheet of paper, much like origami.

Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. ( ① ) If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms. ( ② ) In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. ( ③ ) It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. ( ④ ) The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. ( ⑤ ) "The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody," said Prakash.
questions.why: 주어진 문장의 Such a low price(그렇게 낮은 가격)는 ⑤ 바로 앞 문장의 '부품값이 1달러도 안 된다(cost less than a dollar)'를 가리킨다. the whole device는 종이 현미경 Foldscope다.
questions.wrong: ④ 앞에는 현미경이 '비싸서' 쓸 수 없다는 내용과 Foldscope라는 이름만 나와, 낮은 가격을 가리킬 대상이 없다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Everyone who drives, walks, or swipes a transit card in a city views herself as a transportation expert from the moment she walks out the front door. And how she views the street tracks pretty closely with how she gets around. That's why we find so many well-intentioned and civic-minded citizens arguing past one another. At neighborhood meetings in school auditoriums, and in back rooms at libraries and churches, local residents across the nation gather for often-contentious discussions about transportation proposals that would change a city's streets. And like all politics, all transportation is local and intensely personal. A transit project that could speed travel for tens of thousands of people can be stopped by objections to the loss of a few parking spaces or by the simple fear that the project won't work. It's not a challenge of the data or the traffic engineering or the planning. Public debates about streets are typically rooted in emotional assumptions about how a change will affect a person's commute, ability to park, belief about what is safe and what isn't, or the bottom line of a local business.
choices: ① Traffic Data as the Key to Ending Street Disputes
② Neighborhood Meetings: Where Cities Plan Their Streets
③ Why Arguments over Streets Are About Feelings, Not Figures
④ How Faster Transit Wins Public Support
⑤ Every Commuter Is a True Transportation Expert
questions.why: 마지막 두 문장이 핵심이다. 거리 논쟁은 데이터나 교통 공학의 문제가 아니라 감정적인 가정에 뿌리를 둔다. 이것을 '숫자(figures)가 아니라 감정(feelings)'으로 바꿔 말한 ③이 제목이다.
questions.wrong: ① 데이터가 해결책이라는 것은 본문과 반대, ② 주민 회의는 장소일 뿐, ④ 빠른 교통 사업이 오히려 주차 공간 반대로 막힌다고 했다. ⑤ 사람들이 스스로를 전문가로 '여긴다'고 했을 뿐 진짜 전문가라는 말이 아니다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Moral realism represents a philosophical view ①<u>claiming</u> that objective ethical principles exist and should be followed by everyone. The primary task involves identifying clear moral standards through careful analysis and study of human behavior. One must examine various moral statements such as "killing is morally wrong" or "honesty is virtuous" in daily life. Yet, before assessing the truthfulness of such a statement, it is essential to determine whether it is even the kind of statement that can be judged as true or false. If it can ②<u>be</u>, one must then attempt to examine the statement in a real-world context. Such analytical work resembles ③<u>conducting</u> a detailed cost-benefit analysis of actions. It involves weighing negative and positive outcomes ④<u>what</u> specific actions might bring about. Assuming this is possible, then the statement can be said ⑤<u>to possess</u> absolute ethical authority from a moral realist perspective. In other words, truth becomes objective rather than subjective in nature.
questions.why: ④ 앞에 선행사 outcomes가 있고, 뒤의 bring about은 목적어가 빠져 있다. 선행사가 있으므로 관계대명사 that(또는 which)을 써야 하고, 선행사를 포함하는 what은 쓸 수 없다.
questions.wrong: ① 명사 view를 꾸미는 현재분사, ② can be (judged)를 줄인 대동사 be, ③ resemble 뒤 동명사 목적어, ⑤ be said to+동사원형 — 모두 맞다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
Our emotions often outpace our reason, which leads many people to ①<u>confront</u> the ills of the world through feeling and sympathy rather than analysis. Society's response to poverty offers a telling illustration. Instead of tackling the structural roots of deprivation, most efforts concentrate on keeping the poor alive or granting them ②<u>fleeting</u> moments of relief. Such gestures may appear benevolent, yet they frequently leave the central problem untouched and may even ③<u>aggravate</u> it. Paradoxically, these well-meaning acts of charity can turn into ④<u>obstacles</u> to the very transformation that is needed. As long as the foundation is cracked, patching the walls will never keep the rain out. Just as the most humane slave owners unwittingly ⑤<u>undermined</u> a brutal system by rendering it more bearable, those most eager to do good today may end up inflicting the greatest harm.
questions.why: 노예 소유주가 제도를 '견딜 만하게' 만들어 오히려 그 잔인한 제도를 '유지시켰다(sustained/upheld)'는 뜻이어야 한다. undermined(약화시켰다)는 정반대다.
questions.wrong: ① 감정으로 세상의 문제에 맞서다, ② 잠깐의(fleeting) 위안, ③ 문제를 악화시키다(aggravate), ④ 근본 변화의 장애물 — 모두 흐름에 맞다. 어려운 낱말이라고 틀린 것은 아니다.

questions.question:
다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
Cinema is prized not for its capacity to render visible the concealed contours of our reality, but for its capacity to disclose what reality itself conceals — the realm of fantasy. This is why the earliest major theorists of film, almost without exception, denounced the advent of sound and other technical refinements (such as color) that steered film toward realism. Since cinema was a thoroughly fantasmatic art, these refinements were wholly superfluous. Worse still, they could only divert filmmakers and audiences from the fantasmatic dimension of cinema, threatening to reduce film to <u>a mere delivery device for representations of reality</u>. So long as the irrealism of silent black-and-white film prevailed, no one could mistake filmic fantasies for depictions of reality. Sound and color, however, risked fostering precisely that illusion, thereby eroding the very essence of film art. As Rudolf Arnheim observes, "The creative power of the artist can only come into play where reality and the medium of representation do not coincide."
choices: ① a technology that hides the outlines of reality from viewers
② an art form that depends on silence and black-and-white images
③ a medium that merely copies the world instead of conjuring fantasy
④ a tool that frees the artist's creative power from reality
⑤ a device that delivers fantasies more vividly than ever before
questions.why: 영화가 소리·색채로 사실주의 쪽으로 가면, 현실이 감춘 환상을 드러내는 예술이 아니라 현실을 그대로 옮겨 전달하는 도구에 그치게 된다는 뜻이다.
questions.wrong: ① 1문장은 영화가 현실의 윤곽을 드러내는 데 가치가 있는 것이 '아니라'고 했다. ② 무성·흑백은 이론가들이 지키려 한 쪽이다. ④ Arnheim은 현실과 표현 수단이 일치하지 않을 때 창의력이 발휘된다고 했다. ⑤ delivery라는 낱말만 같다.

questions.question:
다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
Climate change is a significant driver of environmental disasters, leading to extreme heat waves, prolonged droughts, and heavy rainfall that often results in severe flooding. In the face of increasing environmental uncertainty, certain companies have begun to capitalize on the situation for financial gain. One notable example is a major pharmaceutical company that introduced a new type of mosquito net to the market. ① As global temperatures rise, it is estimated that between 40 and 60 million people in Africa alone could face an increased risk of getting mosquito-borne diseases like malaria, causing demand for mosquito nets to surge. ② Although providing mosquito nets can be seen as a helpful and even necessary response, the deeper ethical issues involved cannot be ignored. ③ Wealthy nations, which are most responsible for the excessive carbon emissions, continue to benefit from the crisis. ④ Individuals can also cut their own carbon emissions by taking public transportation and using less electricity at home. ⑤ Meanwhile, less-developed countries, which have contributed the least to the current environmental crisis, suffer the most severe consequences. This imbalance highlights the urgent need for climate justice and global accountability.
questions.why: 글은 기후 위기에서 이익을 보는 쪽(부유한 나라·기업)과 피해를 보는 쪽(개발도상국)의 불균형, 그리고 기후 정의를 말한다. ④ 개인의 탄소 줄이기 실천은 이 흐름에서 벗어난다.
questions.wrong: ④는 ③의 carbon emissions를 이어받아 자연스러워 보이지만, ⑤의 Meanwhile은 ③의 부유한 나라와 짝을 이루는 문장이다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Science is often pictured as a race in which only the first runner to cross the line is rewarded, while those who finish second or third go home empty-handed. Yet this picture is exaggerated. Even people who use the image admit that it misses something, because repeating and confirming another team's findings is valued and routinely done. The picture is misleading in another way, too: it suggests that only a few great races are being run at any time. Certainly, some contests, such as the search for the Higgs particle or the creation of high-temperature superconductors, draw the attention of the whole world. But a growing number of contests are made up of many separate parts. For years, researchers expected to find 'the' cure for cancer; today they recognize that cancer comes in many forms, each requiring its own approach. In such fields, scientific competition looks less like a single sprint than ________.
choices: ① a marathon that only the fastest runner can complete
② a set of many races, each with its own winner
③ a contest in which the winner keeps all the rewards
④ a game whose rules are written by its referees
⑤ a test that confirms results already found by others
questions.why: 암 치료처럼 하나의 대회가 여러 부분으로 나뉘어 각각 승자가 생긴다는 내용이므로, 과학 경쟁은 '한 번의 단거리 경주'가 아니라 '저마다 승자가 있는 여러 경주'와 같다.
questions.wrong: ①③ 1등만 보상받는다는 관점은 글이 과장이라고 비판한 것이다. ④ 무관하다. ⑤ 다른 팀의 결과를 확인하는 일(replication)은 본문에 나오지만 결론이 아니다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
In many family-run businesses, younger members often take on extra tasks, such as staying late or handling difficult customers, without being asked. Many observers explain this as a simple strategy: by helping out, the young hope to inherit a share of the business someday. On this view, behavior that looks generous is really driven by self-interest tied to family. Yet something puzzling happens in such families. When the youngest members try to help, older siblings who hold higher positions frequently step in and stop them, insisting on doing the work themselves. Why would anyone refuse free help? The answer may lie in what helping produces. Every visible act of service adds to the helper's standing in the family, and that standing can later be exchanged for support from others. Seen this way, helping is less a gift than ________, which explains why those who already hold rank guard it so closely.
choices: ① a currency of status that is worth competing for
② a duty that older members are eager to hand over
③ a sacrifice made purely for the family's survival
④ a lesson that teaches the young how to serve customers
⑤ a reward given to those who inherit the business
questions.why: 도움을 줄 때마다 집안에서의 지위(standing)가 올라가고, 그 지위는 나중에 다른 사람의 지원과 바꿀 수 있다. 그래서 도움은 선물이라기보다 '경쟁할 가치가 있는 지위의 화폐'이고, 윗사람이 그것을 지키려 한다.
questions.wrong: ② 윗사람은 일을 넘기지 않고 오히려 막는다. ③ 글은 순수한 이타심 설명을 넘어선다. ④ 겉으로 드러난 일만 말한다. ⑤ 상속을 노린다는 것은 글이 먼저 소개한 통념일 뿐이다.

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] Yet the very same offer could be presented in a way that made leaving feel far more costly.

There is substantial evidence that setting a specific purchasing option as the default, meaning it is applied unless an alternative is chosen, greatly increases the likelihood that people will accept it. This effect occurs partly because such a setup creates a sense of ownership even before any purchase is made. People tend to feel the loss of something they believe they owned more strongly than the pleasure of gaining something of equal value. ( ① ) Marketers who understand this psychological tendency often use it to influence consumer behavior in subtle yet effective ways. ( ② ) One example involves an Italian telecommunications company that reduced customer cancellations by changing how choices were presented. ( ③ ) Initially, customers who called to cancel were told they would receive one hundred free calls if they chose to stay. ( ④ ) Later, the message was revised to inform them that one hundred free calls had already been added to their account and would be lost if they canceled. ( ⑤ ) This small change led many to hesitate, since they were unwilling to give up what they now viewed as already theirs.
questions.why: 주어진 문장의 the very same offer는 ④ 바로 앞 문장의 '머물면 무료 통화 100회'를 가리킨다. Yet은 '받는다'에서 '떠나면 잃는다'로 바뀌는 다음 문장을 미리 알린다.
questions.wrong: ③ 앞에는 아직 offer가 나오지 않았다. ⑤에 넣으면 바뀐 메시지가 이미 나온 뒤라 could be presented가 어색하다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
In daily conversation, almost any gathering of people gets called a group. Social psychologists, however, reserve the word for something narrower: two or more people who interact with one another and influence one another. What separates a true group from a mere crowd is this web of mutual dependence directed toward a shared goal. Consider the passengers who ride the same early bus to work every weekday. They may see the same faces for years, yet they rarely speak, coordinate, or rely on one another, so in the strict sense they do not form a group. Compare them with the members of a community choir who meet every Thursday evening. Each singer must listen to the others, adjust pitch and volume to blend in, and follow the conductor's cues, all for the sake of a performance they will give together. It is precisely this joining of individuals around a common purpose that turns a collection of people into a team.

[요약문] To social psychologists, people form a group not merely by __(A)__ the same space but by __(B)__ one another in pursuit of a shared goal.
choices: ① leaving … observing
② sharing … influencing
③ sharing … observing
④ avoiding … influencing
⑤ leaving … ignoring
questions.why: 같은 버스를 타는 승객은 공간만 함께할 뿐 서로 말하거나 의지하지 않으므로 집단이 아니다. 합창단처럼 공동 목표를 위해 서로 '영향을 주고받아야(influencing)' 집단이 된다. (A) sharing, (B) influencing.
questions.wrong: ③ observing — 승객들이 몇 년간 같은 얼굴을 '보지만' 집단은 아니다. ①⑤ leaving, ④ avoiding은 같은 공간에 있다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Scientists have no special purchase on moral or ethical decisions; a climate scientist is no more qualified to comment on health care reform than a physicist ①<u>does</u> to judge the causes of bee colony collapse. The very features that create expertise in a specialized domain ②<u>lead</u> to ignorance in many others. In some cases lay people — farmers, fishermen, patients, native peoples — may have relevant experiences ③<u>that</u> scientists can learn from. Indeed, in recent years, scientists have begun to recognize this: the Arctic Climate Impact Assessment includes observations ④<u>gathered</u> from local native groups. So our trust needs to be limited, and focused. It needs to be very particular. Blind trust will get us into at least as much trouble as no trust at all. But without some degree of trust in our designated experts — the men and women who have devoted their lives to ⑤<u>sorting</u> out tough questions about the natural world we live in — we are paralyzed, in effect not knowing whether to make ready for the morning commute or not.
questions.why: 앞 절의 동사가 is (qualified)이므로 뒤에서 되받는 대동사도 is여야 한다. does는 일반동사를 받을 때 쓴다.
questions.wrong: ② 주어는 The very features(복수)라 lead가 맞다. 바로 앞 domain에 끌려 leads로 착각하기 쉽다. ③ learn from의 목적어가 빠진 관계대명사, ④ '수집된' 관찰이므로 과거분사, ⑤ devote ~ to 뒤 동명사.

questions.question:
다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
Trends toward a marked increase in competition have forced companies to adopt much more aggressive innovation strategies. Innovation provides one way of getting out of the competition, which is to say situations in which activities are not very profitable. ① Innovation indeed provides an opportunity to set oneself apart and temporarily to assume a monopoly position; this provides an opportunity to make a profit either by increasing prices or by reducing costs. ② Still, companies that keep innovating tend to earn less than those that simply wait for their rivals to fail. ③ There are, of course, other means that can be relied upon to survive and prosper in a market economy. ④ These conventional means rely mainly on geographical distances and transportation costs, the limited capacity of consumers to compare prices and qualities fully, and the existence of regulated activities. ⑤ All these mechanisms reduce the degree of competition and allow companies to survive even if they do not have the best product or the cheapest price. However, globalization, deregulation, and some antitrust policies are all trends which dramatically weaken the effectiveness of those conventional means. Innovative strategies, therefore, appear as the only way to survive and prosper in the new competitive environment.
questions.why: 글의 결론은 '혁신만이 살아남는 유일한 길'이다. ② '계속 혁신하는 기업이 덜 번다'는 이 주장을 뒤집는다. ②를 빼면 ① 혁신의 이익 → ③ 다른 수단(other means)으로 자연스럽게 이어진다.
questions.wrong: ⑤ All these mechanisms는 ④의 전통적 수단들을 정리하는 문장으로 흐름에 맞다.

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] There is, however, one condition attached to this freedom.

Traditional copyright works like a fence around a private garden: it protects creators' income by letting them alone decide who may enter, pick, or replant what grows there. Behind the fence lies a belief that people plant more seeds when they can be sure the harvest will be theirs. ( ① ) The "copyleft" movement, however, pulls this belief up by its roots. ( ② ) Its supporters argue that creativity grows best in an open field, where anyone is free to take a cutting and grow something new from it. ( ③ ) Unlike copyright, which locks the gate to protect individual profit, copyleft requires that anyone who changes a work keep the new version open to the public. ( ④ ) As a result, every improvement becomes a seed for the whole community rather than a crop for a single owner. ( ⑤ ) Many open-source software projects show how quickly such shared gardens can bloom into rapid technical progress and wide social benefit. In short, while copyright guards private gains, copyleft treats shared knowledge as the soil in which social progress grows.
questions.why: 주어진 문장의 this freedom은 ③ 앞 문장의 '누구나 자유롭게 가지를 꺾어 새로 키울 수 있다'를 받는다. one condition은 ③ 뒤 문장의 조건(바꾼 작품은 공개해야 한다)을 예고한다.
questions.wrong: ② 앞에서는 아직 '자유'가 나오지 않았다. ④는 조건이 이미 나온 뒤다.

questions.question:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
A field sown with an old local variety of wheat may look like a sea of identical plants, yet its stalks differ slightly from one another in their genes. On a calm, sunny day, these small differences seem to matter little.

(A) A field planted from a single, uniform modern variety has no such reserve. If one pest arrives that the variety cannot resist, every plant falls together, like a row of dominoes.

(B) They begin to matter the moment conditions change — when a new disease sweeps in, when the rains fail, or when temperatures climb. Under such pressure, plants whose genes happen to suit the new conditions survive and leave more seeds, so the field slowly reshapes itself over generations. In this way, genetic variety works as a reserve the field can draw on in hard times.

(C) A mixed field, by contrast, loses some plants but not the harvest. This is why farmers who keep old local varieties are protecting more than tradition: they are keeping the field's ability to recover.
questions.why: (B) They begin to matter는 주어진 글의 '별로 중요해 보이지 않는다(seem to matter little)'를 이어받는다. (A) no such reserve는 (B) 끝의 a reserve를 받는다. (C) by contrast는 (A)의 단일 품종 밭과 대비된다.
questions.wrong: ③ (B) 다음에 (C) mixed field를 바로 붙이기 쉽지만, by contrast로 대비할 단일 품종 밭이 (A)에 있으므로 (A)가 먼저다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Studies of clothing usually follow a garment along a straight road: it is bought, worn, washed, and finally thrown away. Within this picture, mending a torn seam or replacing a button simply adds a few more miles before the inevitable end. Some researchers, however, question whether a coat really has a 'biography' with a beginning, a middle, and an end. A jacket may be worn daily for a winter, then forgotten in a closet for years, then rescued for a costume party, cut down into a child's vest, and finally sold at a flea market to someone in another city. Some garments are even taken apart so that their buttons and zippers can live on in other clothes. Each of these turns gives the object a new use and a new owner. In other words, the life of a thing is better imagined as ________ than as a single line drawn from the shop to the trash can.
choices: ① a straight road leading to a fixed destination
② a story that ends when its first owner loses interest
③ a product whose value depends on its original price
④ a circle that always returns to its starting point
⑤ a winding path with many returns and detours
questions.why: 재킷이 입히고, 잊히고, 다시 쓰이고, 고쳐지고, 팔리는 과정을 보면 물건의 삶은 직선이 아니라 '여러 번 되돌아오고 돌아가는 구불구불한 길'이다.
questions.wrong: ① 1문장의 straight road는 글이 비판하는 관점이다. ④ 물건은 같은 출발점으로 돌아오지 않고 새 용도·새 주인으로 간다. ②③ 본문에 근거가 없다.

questions.question:
다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
A literary critic once compared two ways of understanding how people remember their own lives: psychology, he said, is a well-kept garden, while literature is a wild forest. The image is apt. Psychologists prune and arrange; they look for rules that hold across many people and trim away whatever refuses to fit. Novelists and poets, on the other hand, plunge into the tangled, uncontrollable undergrowth of experience. The same contrast applies to research on young children. A researcher who cares only about orderly stages and predictable responses may overlook something that runs through almost everything children say and do: their playful, irregular, often bizarre habits of mind. Wild, personal thinking is not a privilege of trained writers; a four-year-old inventing a talking cloud is doing it too. Anyone who wants an honest portrait of how children think, then, must sometimes <u>leave the trimmed paths and walk among the weeds</u>.
choices: ① explore children's unpredictable, imaginative thinking instead of only seeking regular patterns
② train children to replace their fantasies with orderly, logical reasoning
③ borrow the methods of novelists to write stories about children
④ remove the irregular data that do not fit established developmental stages
⑤ observe children playing outdoors rather than in laboratories
questions.why: '다듬어진 길(trimmed paths)'은 규칙과 단계를 찾는 심리학, '잡초 속(weeds)'은 아이들의 불규칙하고 상상력 넘치는 생각이다. 아이들을 제대로 이해하려면 규칙만 찾지 말고 그런 생각도 탐구해야 한다는 뜻이다.
questions.wrong: ②④ 아이들의 생각을 질서에 맞추거나 잘라내는 것은 글과 반대다. ③ 소설을 쓰라는 뜻이 아니다. ⑤ weeds를 진짜 야외로 읽은 것이다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
In moments of crisis, many of us were taught to keep a straight face. A calm exterior, the thinking goes, proves we are strong, while tears or a trembling voice only add fuel to the fire. But this silent rule ignores what speaking our feelings actually does. Putting a vague fear into words forces us to sort it, name it, and place it in order, so the fog inside the mind begins to thin. Spoken feelings also act as a signal flare: they show colleagues, friends, and family exactly where help is needed. Researchers have found that people who receive such help bounce back more readily when hardship strikes again and again. By contrast, those who bottle up their distress carry an unpaid bill that grows with interest, sometimes coming due later as anxiety or depression. In short, showing our emotions during hard times is not a crack in the wall but ________.
choices: ① a sign that the wall was never strong enough
② a hole that lets others see our weakness
③ a door that should stay shut until the storm passes
④ a beam that holds the whole structure together
⑤ a decoration that hides the damage underneath
questions.why: 감정을 말로 표현하면 생각이 정리되고, 도움을 받을 수 있어 다시 일어서기 쉽다. 그러니 감정 표현은 벽의 '균열'이 아니라 구조를 '떠받치는 기둥(beam)'이다.
questions.wrong: 선지가 모두 벽 비유다. ①②③ 감정 표현을 약점으로 보는 통념 쪽이고, ⑤ 감추는 것이라 글과 반대다.

questions.question:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Sports reporting, especially in printed newspapers, occupies a strangely contradictory place within its own profession. On the one hand, fans (A) [eagerly / rarely] turn to reporters' match descriptions and analysis, and those who cover sport in all its forms rank among the most widely noticed writers of our time. The reflections of a small group of star sports columnists are in great demand at leading papers, and their generous salaries make colleagues on other news desks envious. On the other hand, the regard these writers receive from fellow journalists is far (B) [greater / smaller] than their audiences or earnings would suggest. A worn-out joke still dismisses sport as the 'toy department' of the newsroom, a phrase used to belittle what sports writers produce. The result of this refusal to treat the field seriously is an odd one: sports journalists are widely read yet seldom (C) [respected / ignored].
choices: ① eagerly … greater … respected
② eagerly … smaller … respected
③ eagerly … smaller … ignored
④ rarely … greater … ignored
⑤ rarely … smaller … respected
questions.why: (A) 팬들이 기사를 '열심히(eagerly)' 찾아 읽는다. (B) On the other hand 뒤이므로 동료 기자들의 평가는 독자 수·연봉에 비해 '더 작다(smaller)'. (C) '많이 읽히지만 존중받지(respected) 못한다'는 역설이다.
questions.wrong: ③ (C)에 ignored를 넣으면 '많이 읽히고 무시도 안 된다'가 되어 역설이 사라진다.

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] To see how far it has traveled, we need only begin with the heroes of ancient legend.

Throughout history, the concept of heroism has undergone major changes across different cultures. ( ① ) Classical heroes were traditionally defined as men with a strong commitment to truth and justice, and they willingly sacrificed themselves to protect their communities through quests, battles, and encounters with mythical creatures. ( ② ) Contemporary heroism, however, presents a different landscape where today's heroes are frequently women, which reflects society's evolving understanding of leadership and moral courage in modern times. ( ③ ) Moreover, modern heroic acts emphasize moral strength and ethical decision-making over physical power, highlighting inner strength rather than bravery in battle and combat skills. ( ④ ) Despite these fundamental shifts in how we perceive and define heroes, their essential function remains unchanged. ( ⑤ ) Heroes continue to show the inherent capacity for goodness within every individual. They serve as powerful catalysts that motivate us to extend compassion to others and shape our moral aspirations through their inspiring examples and selfless actions. Ultimately, heroes fulfill a timeless and universal purpose: they inspire each person to pursue their highest potential and become better human beings.
questions.why: 주어진 문장의 it은 1문장의 the concept of heroism이다. '옛 전설 속 영웅부터 살펴보자(begin with)'는 예고이므로 고전 영웅 설명이 시작되기 바로 앞인 ①이 알맞다.
questions.wrong: ② 자리는 옛 영웅 설명이 이미 끝난 뒤라 '~부터 시작하자'가 어색하다. ④⑤ 부분은 변화가 아니라 '변하지 않는 기능'을 말한다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Ask what a person ought to learn, and anthropologists have a ready reply: it depends on where that person lives. Knowledge that is essential in one community may be useless in another, so there is no universal list of lessons that every human being must master. Yet this observation hides a less comfortable consequence. Differences between cultures can only be noticed if, inside each culture, people learn largely the same things; a society whose members each studied whatever they pleased would have no recognizable culture to compare. For that reason, no community leaves the choice of learning entirely to the individual. Nowhere on earth may a person learn simply anything he or she wishes. And it is the school, founded by the community rather than by the family, that sees to it that each member acquires what the group requires.

[요약문] Although what people must learn __(A)__ from one culture to another, every society expects its members to __(B)__ a shared body of knowledge, and it relies on schools to make sure they do.
choices: ① differs … question
② expands … adopt
③ remains … select
④ differs … select
⑤ differs … adopt
questions.why: 무엇을 배워야 하는지는 문화마다 '다르지만(differs)', 문화 차이가 드러나려면 각 사회 안에서 사람들이 대체로 같은 것을 배워야 한다. 그래서 사회는 구성원이 공통 지식을 '받아들이기(adopt)'를 요구하고, 학교가 그 일을 맡는다.
questions.wrong: ④ select(스스로 고르다)는 '누구도 원하는 것을 마음대로 배울 수 없다'는 본문과 반대다. ③ remains도 본문과 반대다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Why animals sleep at all is still one of biology's open questions. One answer treats sleep as a repair shift: the body closes for maintenance, and creatures that burn energy quickly, needing more repairs, stay closed longer. A second answer looks not inside the body but at the world around it. On this view, sleep is a luxury that each species can afford only after its other bills are paid. An elephant, which must spend most of the day feeding its enormous frame, has little time left over and sleeps only briefly. A lion, which fears almost no one, can doze for hours, and so can a bat hanging in a dark cave or a rodent tucked inside its burrow. Horses and cattle, too large to hide and too tempting to predators, keep their naps short. Indeed, when many species are compared, an animal's size and the danger it faces explain much of how long it sleeps. In this sense, the length of an animal's sleep may depend less on ________ than on what its surroundings allow.
choices: ① the dangers it meets during the day
② how much repair its body requires
③ the amount of food it can easily find
④ the size of the animals that hunt it
⑤ how hidden its sleeping place is
questions.why: 'less on ___ than on what its surroundings allow' 구조이므로, 빈칸에는 '주변 환경'과 대비되는 몸 안의 요인, 즉 몸이 필요로 하는 회복의 양이 들어간다.
questions.wrong: ①③④⑤는 모두 본문에 나온 환경 요인(위험, 먹이, 포식자, 은신처)이다. 내용은 맞지만 구조상 빈칸에 들어갈 수 없다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
What happens to us during the day has a strong influence on what we dream at night and how those dreams feel. Stressful moments such as a conflict at work or a personal setback often come back in our dreams, though in changed scenes. While we sleep, the brain reworks the day's memories, often turning real events into symbolic or exaggerated stories. Neuroscientists have found that experiences full of emotion are far more likely to enter our dreams than neutral ones. That is why we dream about a recent argument, surprising news, or a big change in our lives, but rarely about brushing our teeth or checking e-mail. Why should the mind be so choosy? One explanation is that sleep is not a time for storing everything but for sorting what still matters. An argument that ended without resolution is an open file; brushing one's teeth was closed the moment it was done. By replaying the open files in new and often strange settings, the dreaming brain lets us test reactions we never tried while awake, at no real cost if they fail. Seen in this light, dreams are less a random replay of the day than ________.
choices: ① a faithful recording of everything we did while awake
② an escape from the stressful events of daily life
③ a rehearsal stage for events we expect tomorrow
④ a reward the brain gives itself for finishing routine tasks
⑤ a workshop for the emotional business the day left unfinished
questions.why: 끝나지 않은 감정(열린 파일)을 꿈속 새로운 장면에서 되돌려 보며 반응을 시험해 본다고 했으므로, 꿈은 낮에 끝내지 못한 감정의 일을 처리하는 '작업장(workshop)'이다.
questions.wrong: ① 꿈은 모든 것을 기록하지 않고 골라낸다. ② 스트레스 사건은 꿈에 다시 나온다. ③ 시험해 보는 대상은 '지난' 일이지 내일 일이 아니다. ④ 양치처럼 반복되는 일은 꿈에 잘 나오지 않는다.

questions.question:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
Organizations today are drowning in data — every online purchase, social media post, and sensor reading adds another drop to an ocean that never stops rising.

(A) Yet owning an ocean of data is not the same as knowing what lies beneath its surface. Raw records, left alone, answer no questions; they simply pile up. Someone, or something, has to ask them.

(B) As the ocean deepens, diving by hand becomes impossible, and the need for such tools only grows. An organization without them is like a ship anchored over sunken treasure it cannot reach: rich on paper, poor in practice. For any organization that hopes to stay competitive, learning to mine its data is no longer a choice.

(C) That is the task of data mining, which dives into vast datasets to bring up patterns, links, and trends no human eye would catch. Retailers use it to anticipate what customers will want next, and hospitals use it to spot signs of illness hidden in thousands of patient records.
questions.why: (A) Yet은 '데이터가 넘친다'를 뒤집는다. (C) That is the task는 (A) 끝의 '누군가 질문해야 한다'를 받는다. (B) such tools와 them은 (C)의 data mining을 가리키므로 마지막이다.
questions.wrong: (B)의 As the ocean deepens가 주어진 글의 ocean과 이어지는 것처럼 보이지만, such tools가 가리킬 대상이 (C)에 있으므로 (B)는 맨 뒤다.

questions.passage: As concern for the planet spreads, a growing number of companies dress their products in green clothing to win over eco-minded shoppers. This practice, called "greenwashing," is less a change of heart than a change of costume: firms (a) <u>inflate</u> or even invent environmental claims so that they look far greener than they really are. A bottle stamped "organic" or "biodegradable" with no evidence behind the label is like a window painted on a solid wall — it promises a view that does not exist. Shoppers who buy such products may believe they are planting trees when they are only (b) <u>scattering</u> seeds on concrete. The deeper damage, however, is done to trust, which works like a shared well in a village: once someone poisons it, everyone stops drinking, even from the clean buckets. Consumers who learn they have been fooled tend to (c) <u>embrace</u> honest green claims as well, so genuine efforts lose the customers they deserve. The remedy is not to stop buying but to buy with open eyes. Checking for third-party certification or (d) <u>reliable</u> data turns each purchase into a vote that can be (e) <u>counted</u>, and such informed choices are what keep real environmental responsibility alive.

questions.question: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: ① Green Labels: A Reliable Guide for Smart Shoppers
② Why Organic Products Cost More Than They Should
③ How Companies Change Their Hearts to Save the Planet
④ A Green Costume That Poisons the Well of Trust
⑤ Planting Trees: The Best Way to Help the Environment
questions.why: 기업이 '마음'이 아니라 '옷'만 녹색으로 갈아입는다(costume), 그리고 신뢰라는 '우물에 독을 푼다'는 두 비유를 합친 제목이다.
questions.wrong: ① 녹색 라벨은 믿을 수 없다는 것이 글의 내용이다. ② 가격 이야기는 없다. ③ 글은 change of heart가 '아니라'고 했다. ⑤ planting trees는 비유를 글자 그대로 읽은 것이다.

questions.question: 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: ① (a)
② (b)
③ (c)
④ (d)
⑤ (e)
questions.why: 속은 소비자는 정직한 환경 주장까지 '불신하게(distrust)' 된다. 그래야 뒤의 '진짜 노력이 고객을 잃는다'와 이어진다. embrace(받아들이다)는 반대다.
questions.wrong: (a) 부풀리다, (b) 콘크리트에 씨를 뿌리다(헛수고), (d) 믿을 만한 자료, (e) 반영되는 표 — 모두 흐름에 맞다.
